nomenclature.etymology_html:
- Aegle : In Greek mythology Aegle was one of the Naiads (nymphs of the fresh water, rivers, springs and lakes).
- Marmelos : From the Portuguese vernacular name marmelo for marmalade.

stem_bark.text: The bark of Aegle marmelos is greyish-coloured, rough. It is longitudinally fissured.
stem_bark.text_html: The bark of Aegle marmelos is greyish-coloured, rough. It is longitudinally fissured.

seed.text: The seeds of Aegle marmelos are hairy, oblong and whitish-coloured. The seeds are 0.8-1 cm across. They are embedded in a fibrous and orange pulp. There are 10-15 seeds per fruit.
seed.text_html: The seeds of Aegle marmelos are hairy, oblong and whitish-coloured. The seeds are 0.8-1 cm across. They are embedded in a fibrous and orange pulp. There are 10-15 seeds per fruit.

fruit.text: The fruit of Aegle marmelos is a rounded, pyriform or oval berry . The fruit is 10-20 in diameter and woody. It is greenish-coloured turning yellow when fully ripe. The fruit contains 10-15 seeds.
fruit.text_html: The fruit of Aegle marmelos is a rounded, pyriform or oval berry. The fruit is 10-20 in diameter and woody. It is greenish-coloured turning yellow when fully ripe. The fruit contains 10-15 seeds.

leaf.text: The leaves of Aegle marmelos are fascicled on short protuberances. The leaf is compound, 3-foliate. The leaf is 10-12 cm long and 5-8 cm wide with a 3 cm long petiole. The leaflet of Aegle marmelos is ovate, the apex is acuminate, the base is rounded and the margins are slightly serrate. The terminal leaflet are 7-8 cm long and 3.5-4 cm wide with a 0.8-1 cm long petiolule . The 2 lateral ones are subsessile, about 5 cm long and 2.5-3 cm wide. The venation of the leaflets is reticulate with a prominent midrib.
leaf.text_html:
The leaves of Aegle marmelos are fascicled on short protuberances.
The leaf is compound, 3-foliate. The leaf is 10-12 cm long and 5-8 cm wide with a 3 cm long petiole.
The leaflet of Aegle marmelos is ovate, the apex is acuminate, the base is rounded and the margins are slightly serrate.
The terminal leaflet are 7-8 cm long and 3.5-4 cm wide with a 0.8-1 cm long petiolule. The 2 lateral ones are subsessile, about 5 cm long and 2.5-3 cm wide.
The venation of the leaflets is reticulate with a prominent midrib.

habit.text: Aegle marmelos is a thorny, small-sized and decideous tree growing up to 10-12 m high.
habit.text_html: Aegle marmelos is a thorny, small-sized and decideous tree growing up to 10-12 m high.

reproduction_dispersal.text: Aegle marmelos is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures). Aegle marmelos is pollinated by a wide variety of insects. The seeds of Aegle marmelos are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.
reproduction_dispersal.text_html:
• Sex distribution :

    Aegle marmelos is bisexual (each flower of each individual has both male and female structures).

  • Mode of pollination :

    Aegle marmelos is pollinated by a wide variety of insects.

  • Seed dispersal :

    The seeds of Aegle marmelos are mainly dispersed by frugivorous birds and mammals.

veterinary.text: The leaves and twigs of Aegle marmelos are lopped for fodder.
veterinary.text_html: The leaves and twigs of Aegle marmelos are lopped for fodder.

handicrafts.text: The wood of Aegle marmelos is hard and takes a good polish. It is used for house building, carving, agricultural implements or tool handles... A yellow dye is obtained from the rind of the unripe fruit. It is used in calico printing. An essential oil is extracted from the rind. The gum makes a good adhesive. The fruit pulp has detergent action and has been used for washing clothes. Source : - Dastur, 2006, Useful Plants of India and Pakistan - Orwa C., Mutua A., Kindt R., Jamnadass R., Anthony S., 2009, Agroforestree Database: a tree reference and selection guide

culinary.text: Aegle marmelos fruit pulp is edible. The pulp mixed with milk and sugar makes a popular drink in India.
culinary.text_html:
Aegle marmelos fruit pulp is edible.
The pulp mixed with milk and sugar makes a popular drink in India.

reforestation.text: Aegle marmelos prefers full sun. It is drought resistant and it will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils but all soils need to be free draining. The species is propagated by seeds. 24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
reforestation.text_html:
• Planting advice and requirements :

    Aegle marmelos prefers full sun. It is drought resistant and it will grow in a wide variety of situations and soils but all soils need to be free draining.
    The species is propagated by seeds.

  • Seed treatments :

    24 hours of soaking in water accelerates the germination process.
